Only CHANGELOG.md was supplied (base lines 1381-1756, head lines 1-232). It is documentation with no executable change, so no regression, new attack surface or invalidated assumption is visible in these units. The head entries describe behavior that lives in unsupplied files, so the next pass should check that code in the other batch units against the cited threat IDs.

1. SSD prefix cache (T-041, SEC-035, A-001), head lines 5-10. The entries describe retaining a distinct demanded shared-prefix checkpoint, giving authenticated repeated checkpoints a first-appearance share of the reserved SSD write budget, and bounding COMPLETE donation hashing. Check three points in the cache code: lookup tags stay HMAC-only, cacheSalt scoping stays account-bound, and the 30-minute TTL and per-donation gate are unchanged. Also confirm the new write-share priority cannot be used by a same-account caller to widen the timing oracle or evade the endurance ledger (lines 61-62).

2. Autopilot daily earnings floor (A-009, TB-006), head lines 18-22. This adds a new financial surface: a funded floor pool, admin funding and baseline-repair endpoints, a baseline frozen from the preceding 168 hours that includes sponsored inference, and consent evidence. Review for sybil or self-dealing inflation of the baseline, atomic idempotent daily receipts, and admin-key gating. The threat model has no entry for this feature. The new financial tables are not covered by the existing accounting archives, as the entry itself notes.

3. Account erasure and soft-delete (T-059, A-009), head lines 102-120 and 91-96. The entries cover the new mutation gate, erasure fences, and the Stripe outbox. Verify that the gate returns 503 after authorization and that late credits cannot reach erased accounts.

4. Migrations (head lines 91-94, 138-146). Verify the migration deadline and index-lock behavior, and the rollback compatibility notes.

Other items: machine-scoped Autopilot (lines 28-33), model diagnostics (lines 24-26) and the review-gating entries (lines 45-53). Release-integrity statements are claims only, not evidence.
